paper_title: Memorization and Knowledge Injection in Gated LLMs
caption: Analysis on the embedding quality in Llama intermediate layers. Correct gate rate is computed as the rate of question embeddings which have the maximum inner product with the relevant passage embedding. It is computed for each dataset partition, which has 50 passage samples. Shaded area is the standard deviation across 20 dataset partitions. We found that embeddings at the input of MLP layers are better than at the input of attention layers. We choose to use last MLP layer input as embedding in the main experiments of MEGa.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between embedding layer and average correct gate rate for different input types and layer architectures. The x-axis, labeled “Embedding Layer,” is linear, ranging from 0 to 30 with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “Average Correct Gate Rate,” is linear, ranging from 0.2 to 1.0 with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. A solid blue line represents “Character Attention input,” starting at approximately 0.2 and rising to a peak of about 0.75 at an embedding layer of 5 before decreasing to around 0.55 at an embedding layer of 30. A dashed blue line represents “Character MLP input,” beginning at approximately 0.75 and remaining between 0.8 and 0.95 across the entire range of the x-axis, eventually decreasing slightly to about 0.85 at an embedding layer of 30. A solid red line signifies “Wiki Attention input,” beginning at 0.2 and increasing to a maximum of about 0.85 at an embedding layer of 15, then decreasing to approximately 0.6 at an embedding layer of 30. A dashed red line indicates “Wiki MLP input,” starting at approximately 0.75 and remaining fairly constant between 0.8 and 0.9 across the x-axis, ending at a value of around 0.87 at an embedding layer of 30. Each line is accompanied by a shaded region representing the standard deviation.
